title: Morning gratitude
hook: one thing you're glad of on waking
tomorrow: an emperor lists who will annoy him today. why on earth?

segments.voice: Yesterday, move first: Thoreau's dawn swim in Walden Pond, which he called a religious exercise. The body is up. Today, the first words.

Dread can wake up before you do: the inbox, the bill, yesterday's hard thing still waiting. The poet of Lamentations woke up to worse. Jerusalem had fallen, and the book is a long cry over the ruins. Then, in the middle of it, he says: "It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."
screen: `DREAD BEFORE YOUR FEET HIT THE FLOOR.` → `A POET IN A RUINED CITY.` → `NEW EVERY MORNING.`

segments.voice: Today's question: what should the first words of the day be? Jewish tradition answers with a short prayer said on waking, before getting out of bed, before even washing the hands: Modeh Ani, I give thanks. In it you thank God, the living and lasting King, for returning your soul to you with compassion, and it ends with the poet's words from the ruins: great is your faithfulness. Here is the teaching. The Talmud calls sleep a small taste of death, so each waking is a soul given back, a gift, not a given. Gratitude comes first, before you've done anything to earn the day. Not because the day is good yet. The poet said it standing in rubble. The morning itself is the evidence. Now a neighbor. Islam keeps waking words too. Bukhari records that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, would say on waking: praise be to God who gave us life after He had made us die, and to Him is the return. And the Qur'an says God takes souls at death, and takes in sleep the souls that have not died, sending them back for a set term. Shared: sleep as the soul held, waking as the soul returned, thanks as the first word. An honest difference: Modeh Ani dwells on the soul restored and God's faithfulness; the Muslim words also look ahead, to the final return to God. Two prayers, each in its own house.
screen: `WHAT ARE THE FIRST WORDS?` · `MODEH ANI: A SOUL GIVEN BACK.` · `THANKS BEFORE THE DAY EARNS IT.` · `ISLAM'S WAKING WORDS: TO HIM IS THE RETURN.` · then, large: `GLAD TO WAKE.`

segments.voice: Name three things you're glad of right now, under your breath: something in this room, something in your body, someone in your life. Keep each one small and specific, and stay with the third a little longer, the way the old waking prayers give thanks before anything else.
Morning gratitude: thanks as the first word of the day. In Jewish practice, Modeh Ani, for a soul given back.
Your line: glad to wake. The mercies are new before the day has done a thing. Until tomorrow.
